name: badge
description: A small label that states a fact about the thing beside it — a status, a category, a count. 69 uses across the three surfaces and no two agreed: the website spelled it as a rounded-full span with an alpha tint and an alpha border, the app as a dozen local classes. The tint/ink pairing is the part worth centralising, because an alpha tint over an unknown ground has no guaranteed contrast and every one of them was picked by eye.

tone.$description: A TINT with the tone's ink on it, not a solid fill. The solid form shouts — a row of six filled pills is six things demanding attention — and the tinted form is what the site's own skill cards already used, by hand, at five different alphas. Each tint is a concrete colour with its ink measured on it, because `bg-accent/15` over an unknown ground guarantees nothing.

solid.$description: Filled, for the one badge that must carry across a busy row — a live status in a table of drafts. Rare on purpose: if two badges in a set are solid, neither is.

quiet.$description: An outline and no fill, for a badge that must not compete with the row it sits in.

size.$description: A badge sits beside something, so its ladder is the ladder of the things it labels: a nano badge on a card title, a micro one in a table row, a meta one standing alone.

a11y.note: A badge is a label, not a control. It carries no role — a screen reader reads it as the text it is. When the badge is the ONLY thing saying a row failed, the row needs the word too: colour is never the only signal.
